Bench: Abhinand Kumar Shavili
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice Abhinand Kumar Shavili
 And
The Hon'Ble Sri Justice Vakiti Ramakrishna Reddy
 Land Acquisition Appeal Suit No.666 of 2010
Judgment :

(Per Hon'ble Sri Justice Vakiti Ramakrishna Reddy) This appeal is preferred by the appellant/Land Acquisition Officer aggrieved by the order dated 08.08.2006 (hereinafter will be referred as the 'impugned order') passed by the learned Senior Civil Judge, Karimnagar (for short 'reference court')
in O.P. No.8 of 2003, wherein the market value of the acquired land as fixed by the Land Acquisition Officer was enhanced from Rs.8,000/- per acre to Rs.40,000/- per acre.
2. For the sake of convenience, hereinafter the parties will be referred to as per their status before the reference Court.

BRIEF FACTS:
3. The brief facts of the case are that the agricultural lands of the respondents/claimants situated in Peddurupally hamlet of Chenjerla Village of Manakondur Mandal of Karimnagar District AKS,J &
VRKR, J LAAS_666_2010 were acquired by the Government for the purpose of providing house sites to the weaker sections of Peddurupally hamlet of Chenjerla Village.
Accordingly an award was passed on 31.07.1998 by fixing the market value of acquired lands at Rs.8,000/- per acre.

Having dissatisfied with the fixation of market value by the Land Acquisition Officer, the claimants filed O.P.No.8 of 2003 to enhance the market value of the acquired lands from Rs.8,000/- per acre to Rs.2,00,000/- per acre.
The Land Acquisition Officer opposed the claim made by the claimants and prayed to dismiss the said claim.
The claimants relied upon the oral evidence of PWs 1 and 2 and the documentary evidence under Ex.A1.
On the other hand, the Revenue Divisional Officer, Karimnagar was examined as RW1 and got marked Exs.B1 to B10 on behalf of the respondent.
On considering the rival contentions, the reference court enhanced the market value of acquired lands to Rs.40,000/- per acre from Rs.8,000/- per acre as fixed by the Land Acquisition Officer.
Aggrieved by the same, the Land Acquisition Officer preferred the present Appeal to set aside the impugned order and pass appropriate orders.

sentences.text: Heard both sides and perused the record.
5. Admittedly, the claimant did not prefer any appeal against the impugned order seeking further enhancement of the market value in respect of the acquired lands.

6. Now the point for determination is:
Whether there are any substantial grounds to interfere with the order dated 08.08.2006 passed by the learned Senior Civil Judge, Karimnagar in O.P. No.8 of 2003?
7. Point:

The contention of the learned counsel for the appellant is that the reference court erred in fixing the market value at the rate of Rs.40,000/- per acre by relying on Ex.A1 and that the acquired lands are agricultural lands and whereas Ex.A1 is a small bit of land purchased for the purpose of house site.
It is further contention of the learned counsel for the appellant that the reference court ought to have seen that no comparable sale deeds were filed by the claimants to fix the just compensation.
8. In order to establish his claim, the claimant not only examined himself as PW1 but also relied upon the oral evidence of AKS,J & VRKR, J LAAS_666_2010 PW2 and documentary evidence under Ex.A1.
Ex.A1 is the sale deed dated 27.03.1995 pertaining to Chenjerla Village and PW2 is the vendee under Ex.A1.
Notification under Section 4 (1) of the Act was issued in the year 1996.
PW2 categorically deposed that the acquired lands are rich in fertility and texture having high potentiality and suitable for raising fruit gardens.
PW2 further deposed that acquired lands are very adjacent to village Abadi and the same are useful for house sites due to extension of village towards road where the acquired lands are situated.

As per Ex.A1, PW2 purchased land to an extent of 484 square yards equivalent to Ac.0.4 guntas in Sy.No.828 situated at Chenjerla Village from one Bolla Jagannatha for a valid consideration of Rs.9,700/- which comes to Rs.97,000/- per acre.
9. It is to be seen that even though the lands were acquired on acreage basis the acquired lands were meant for providing house sites to the landless poor.

Further, the claimant relied upon the decision of the Honourable Supreme Court in Ravinder Narain and another v. Union of India1, wherein it was held that rate 1 (2003) 4 SCC 481 AKS,J & VRKR, J LAAS_666_2010 fixed for smaller plots in the same vicinity can be basis for fixation of rate for large area acquired.

entities.text: Ravinder Narain and another v. Union of India1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, the above contention raised by the appellant has already been raised before the reference court and the same was answered by the reference court against the appellant.
Hence, the appellant cannot raise the same ground again before this appellate court.

10. Moreover, in Manilal Shamlbhai Patel (deceased) through his legal heirs and others .v Officer on Special Duty (Land Acquisition) and another2, the Honourable Supreme Court observed as under:
"It is also a settled principle of law that large areas do not attract the same price as is offered for the small plots of lands.
Therefore, some amount of deduction is also normally permissible on account of largeness in area.

Thus, deduction of at least 10%
The Land Acquisition Officer, vs Velichala Satyanarayana on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134615728/
2 has to be applied to determine the rate of compensation."
11. In Ravinder Kumar Goel v. State of Haryana and others3 the Honourable Supreme Court observed as under:
"The position of law is well settled that when large extent of lands are acquired and if the sale exemplar, also for the large extent is available on record it would be safer to rely on the same if they are 2 2025 SCC Online SC 634 3 2023 SCC Online SC 147 AKS,J & VRKR, J LAAS_666_2010 comparable transactions.

sentences.text: However, as already noted above, this Court in Atma Singh (supra) has also held that the sale instances of smaller extents cannot be ignored.
Further, this Court has reiterated in many cases that the sale exemplars for smaller extent can be relied upon subject to appropriate deduction being provided towards development charges."

12. In view of the principle laid down in the above said two decisions, it is amply clear that sale instances of smaller extents cannot be ignored and sale exemplars for smaller extent can be relied upon subject to deduction of at least 10% towards development charges.
13. The sale exemplar relied upon by the claimant under Ex.A1 discloses that an extent of Ac.0.4 guntas of land was purchased for a sale consideration of Rs.9,700/-.
However, the reference court did not enhance the market value of acquired lands by solely relying on Ex.A1.

In fact, the reference court did not consider the rate of land as mentioned in Ex.A1 on the ground that PW2 did not spell out in his evidence about the distance between those lands and the acquired lands.
In the impugned order the reference court observed that the acquired lands are situated in a commercial locality.

Though the reference court did not solely rely upon AKS,J & VRKR, J LAAS_666_2010 Ex.A1, the said document was made as a basis to fix the market value at the rate of Rs.40,000/- per acre on the ground that the acquired lands are also fit for construction of houses and that the acquired lands are having some advantages in terms of location from the Karimnagar Town as that of the land under Ex.A1.

further, the reference court also specifically found that the Land Acquisition Officer did not give proper reasons for fixing prices at the rate of Rs.8,000/- per acre for the acquired lands nor taken into consideration various facts and circumstances to fix the market value particularly the location of the acquired lands from Karimnagar Town and also the potentiality of the acquired lands apart from future expansion etc.

14. The Revenue Divisional Officer, Karimnagar, who was examined as RW1 deposed that the lands acquired are dry lands and that the market value of Rs.8,000/- per acre as fixed by the then Land Acquisition Officer is reasonable and correct.
Ex.B1 is the copy of the award and Exs.B2 to B9 are the pahanies for the years from 1980-81 to 1986-87 and Ex.B10 is the village sketch map of Chenjerla Village.
However, in the cross examination, AKS,J & VRKR, J LAAS_666_2010 RW1 admitted that the acquired lands are situated at a distance of 20 kms from Karimnagar town.
No material is placed on behalf of the respondents to establish that the acquired lands will not fetch more market value than Rs.8,000/- per acre as fixed by the then Land Acquisition Officer.

The claimant relied upon a decision of the Honourable Supreme Court in Special Deputy Collector and another Etc., v. Kurra Sambasiva Rao and others Etc.,4 wherein it was observed that the possibility The Land Acquisition Officer, vs Velichala Satyanarayana on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134615728/
3 of future expansion towards town etc., have to be taken into consideration.

sentences.text: 15. As per the contention of the claimant, there are rice mills, saw mills, oil mills and educational institutions situated very near to the acquired lands.

Though the claimant had claimed for enhancement of acquired lands at the rate of Rs.2,00,000/- per acre, the reference court observed in the impugned order that there is no evidence on record to prove that the market value of the acquired lands by the date of notification was more than Rs.2,00,000/- per acre.

The reference court rightly observed in the impugned order that the acquired lands are also fit for construction of houses and 4 AIR 1997 Supreme Court 2625 AKS,J & VRKR, J LAAS_666_2010 the Land Acquisition Officer had not given proper reasons for fixing the price at Rs.8,000/- per acre for the acquired lands.

sentences.text: 16. In view of the above facts and circumstances, we are of the considered view that the appellant failed to establish any tenable grounds so as to interfere with the well reasoned order passed by the reference court.
Hence, this appeal is devoid of merits and liable to be dismissed.
17. Accordingly, the appeal is dismissed.
In the circumstances, there shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel, pending miscellaneous applications, if any, in the appeal, shall stand closed.
